title: phase-u: Strict managed lint adoption, compatible wheels and CLI reference
description:
## Goal
Deliver strict managed sc-lint 0.8.5, approved dependency/refactor carry-in, #648 CLI-reference delivery and #820 stable-ABI wheels for release 1.8.0. This is the user-requested parallel-execution revision of the local pre-import plan; previous review approvals describe their old commits, not this revision. No new review machinery or product capability is claimed by these plan edits.

## Sprint set / agent level
| Sprint | Scope | Hard prerequisites | Agent level |
|---|---|---|---|
| U.1 | Recovered base and existing carry-in handoff | D6 | fast |
| U.2 | Approved strict policy input | U.1 | normal |
| U.3 | ONE existing-refactor verification batch: CLI / Beads / Composer | U.1 | normal |
| U.4 | Final ABI-aware cross contract | U.2; D4/D5 | frontier |
| U.5 | Managed 0.8.5 kit, adapter and root tooling | U.4 | frontier |
| U.6 | Clap reference generator and website | U.1 | normal |
| U.7 | ABI3 features, Python floor audit, limited API | U.1; D4/D5 | frontier |
| U.8 | Build-once wheels, real install matrix, local rehearsal | U.7 | normal |
| U.9 | Shared delivery wiring and complete phase acceptance | U.3, U.5, U.6, U.8 | frontier |
Agent levels are dispatch requirements, not named people or fixed model IDs. Metadata agent_level is fast/normal/frontier; installed-schema difficulty maps frontier to hard, normal to normal and fast to fast. Do not read layer numbers as serial dependencies.

## Open decisions — not approved defaults
D1 OPEN: propose [line_counts] max_production_lines=1000, no exclusions;175 files passed, max807. User must decide before U.2 closes.
D2 OPEN: propose exact forbidden test literals randlee/team-lead/arch-comp/arch-ccomp/comp/comps/team-lead@example.invalid/ATM_HOME, no production owner for those; canonical owners for SC_COMPOSE_DATA_DIR and SC_COMPOSE_TEMPLATE_DIR in template_store.rs, and SC_COMPOSE_TEMPLATE_CONTRACTS_SCOPE in commands/template_lint.rs. Policy input and identity/boundary test drivers consume ONE canonical non-Rust JSON fixture. repo_boundaries.rs:206 must load ATM_HOME from it, not concat! or a lint exemption. User must approve before encoding/closure. No policy is presumed approved and no justified exception is currently proposed.

D3 OPEN — #787 owner: lead/user decides and U.1 records the disposition; if approved, recovery writer comp includes the approved opt-in compatibility layer ending at e8143961 in the approved L1 recovery base, otherwise omits/defers #787; original default-on 588ab3d7 must not ship unchanged.
D4 OPEN — #820: confirm CPython >=3.9 floor; the issue requests it, this plan does not assume approval.
D5 OPEN — #820: should sc-sha-python and sc-composer-beads-python also migrate to abi3? Conditional paths/checks do not presume yes.
D6 OPEN — lead/user selects recovery route A or B under landing rule L1, with exact approved base provenance.
D7 OPEN — proposed v1.7.0 backward-compatibility gate in U.9 needs user approval/disposition; pending is not PASS.

## 1.8.0 issue ledger
| Issue | Owner / outcome |
|---|---|
| #648 | U.6 generator/site, U.9 actual offline installer/release/check wiring; required |
| #817 | Existing #839 carry-in in U.1, verified in final graph by U.9; no waiver/parser redesign |
| #820 | U.7 ABI and U.8 real wheel installs, U.9 shared preflight wiring; required |
| #819 | Superseded; close when #820 lands, no separate per-cp314 project |
Use planned/1.8.0 during planning; released/1.8.0 only at actual publication after Phase U. No publish/release sprint or issue mutation in this local edit.

## Wheel failures: observed vs coverage
- Build cause: the existing release build action defaults to CPython 3.11 and the bindings do not enable abi3, yielding cp311-cp311 wheels. That fixed-version ABI is why a 3.14 binary-wheel resolver cannot use them. Enabling abi3 is the fix; building six separate version-specific wheels is not required. A fixed build interpreter remains valid when the emitted ABI floor/tag is correct.
- #611 reports a concrete pip download sc-compose==1.6.1 --python-version 3.14 --only-binary=:all: resolution failure; published artifacts were cp311-cp311, not abi3: https://github.com/randlee/sc-compose/issues/611 .
- #611 reports a locally built 1.7.0 extension failing import on one macOS 27 / arm64 / Homebrew Python 3.14.7 setup; the later correction explicitly leaves linker/loader root cause unconfirmed: https://github.com/randlee/sc-compose/issues/611#issuecomment-6344556681 . Published cp311 wheel import was reported working in Python 3.11.13.
- #820 reports installer rejection/PATH-dependent selection when host Python differs from the existing 3.11 requirement, motivating a >=3.9 wheel contract: https://github.com/randlee/sc-compose/issues/820 .
The 4 platforms x CPython 3.9-3.14 = 24 cells, each pip+uv, are requested compatibility coverage, NOT 24 reproduced failures. This plan edit did not rerun those historical reproductions. Intel macOS/Windows ARM wheel gaps in #611 remain triage candidates, not added release targets.

## Ledger candidates — user triage pending, NOT committed sprints
One read of gh issue list --state open supplied the following candidates. Titles are evidence of reported defects, not fresh reproduction or an approved fix commitment.
| Issue | Reported defect / triage question |
|---|---|
| #169 | Quadratic rejection latency for deeply nested var-file input |
| #601 | release-preflight package-check-plan generator crash silently passes |
| #615 | Bead render rejects missing .beads/formulas directory |
| #818 | frontmatter-init relative --file fails with empty canonicalized root |
| #611 | Wheel compatibility/platform coverage; overlap with #820, with macOS Intel/Windows ARM requests outside #820's current four-platform matrix |
| #505 | Release notes template not consumed by automation |
| #502 | Release-note included-packages table missing sc-sha and Scoop |
| #357 | temp_root non-RAII leaks reported across test files |
| #240 | Config parse diagnostics lack path/line/column attribution |
| #361 | Old sc-lint boundary helper cargo-runs absent consumer package; triage whether U.5 resolves it, not a new sprint |
These remain candidates until user triage; no auto-close, label change or scope admission. #613/#614 are already labeled shipped/1.7.0 in the issue listing and are not newly scheduled defects. #503 is an ATM ownership report, not admitted to this standalone toolchain.

## Follow-on only
Held toml1, quick-xml0.42, MiniJinja3, clap/serde/thiserror and duplicate-version upgrades remain out of scope. No 1.7.1 changelog/metadata wholesale replay or advisory/identity/size/Clippy exception.
design:
## Boundary map
- BOUNDARY-ScCompose owns sc-lint process invocation/normalization/report HTML and root developer orchestration; sc-lint owns rules and envelopes. Preserve fixed executable/allowlisted descriptors (ADR0016/0017).
- BOUNDARY-ScComposer stays pure: private completed composition/extraction/schema changes preserve API/diagnostic/span semantics; no CLI/ATM dependencies.
- BOUNDARY-ScComposerBeads retains host-neutral argv/receipts/graph/quoting; no test-support dependency reintroduction (ADR0021/0023).
- Directed edges stay CLI->composer/beads, beads->composer, composer->sc-sha, Python/Go adapters->owned libraries. Inventory corrections#836, Zlib removal#837, dev-edge removal#838, YAML advisory repair#839, generator repair#840 and stale workspace cleanup#841 are finished inputs, not new scope.

## Landing rules — sole owner (L1-L4)
L1. Lead/user chooses the clean base before carry-in: A, approved revert-forward recovery PR lands develop first and integrate/phase-u is cut from that recorded corrected head; OR B, authorized rebuild of integrate/phase-u from v1.7.0=f4fda4b9 plus approved replay. Record exact SHA/tree/ancestry and D3 disposition. caa43cfc is contaminated, and acf55fba is not approved as-is with unchanged #787. Reuse the existing recovery epic; do not ordinary-merge quarantined strict-only ancestry.
L2. After L1 and settlement/classification of the known CI exit3 question, comp lands the frozen #831 plus the 17 #825 rows EARLY onto integrate/phase-u, #831 first. This does not wait for U.9. Preserve original QA, source/replay mappings and authorized adaptation/drop dispositions in U.1's sole table. Old 0.4.0 setup may remain red after #836 until U.5 fixes the kit; that is not final acceptance.
L3. One authorized stack writer acts at a time; independent developers work in isolated worktrees and deliver disjoint paths. Layer numbers/PR lower bounds do not impose serial development. Lead coordinates authorized composition/relink and records changed heads. Frozen source is not silently rewritten; confirmed defects receive reviewed corrective work. After U.1, comp is the landing writer for the approved 25 refactor deltas plus #842 onto integrate/phase-u before U.3 verifies that exact candidate; U.3 failures route to a corrective layer, whose unresolved findings block U.9 rather than being fixed by the read-only verifier.
L4. Only the single phase-to-develop PR/phase closure waits for exact-head U.9 aggregate, whole-phase review and explicit user go-ahead. Final sync must preserve the approved clean lineage: A uses corrected develop; B uses the lead/user-approved reconciliation, never blindly merges contaminated develop back. Freeze source/target heads and use full endpoint diff plus replay provenance, rerunning affected final checks if candidate changes. No direct sprint/dependency PR lands develop. Publishing occurs after Phase U.

## Parallel execution and file ownership
After U.1, dispatch U.2/U.3/U.6/U.7 concurrently. U.3 is read-only over a fixed candidate, with three crate sections in one batch. U.2->U.4->U.5 owns root policy/cross/managed files; U.4 uses explicit D4/D5 decisions without waiting for U.7 implementation; U.9 executes the declared rows against that ABI code. U.6 owns only generator/CLI docs/site files and uses existing dependencies, not Cargo.lock. U.7 owns binding sources/manifests and Cargo.lock, no root lint/CI files. U.8 follows U.7's accepted ABI code and owns only wheel-compat.yml/checker/fixtures, not release/ci.yml manifests. U.9 consumes the three real producer contracts to wire shared Justfile/CI/installer/preflight once. This is why U.6 and U.7 have no dependency on one another or U.5.
Planned critical path 5 (U.1->U.2->U.4->U.5->U.9); width 4; 9 sprints. The previous graph had critical path 8 and 11 sprints; this is a dependency count, not a claim about elapsed implementation time. Shared paths always have a real dependency path, not a fabricated serial edge between unrelated features. No U.6->U.7 documentation-to-ABI edge or required throwaway 0.8.4 cross success.

## Evidence lifetime — sole owner (E1-E3)
E1. U.1's one table serves the authorized carry-in writer and U.9 reviewer, gating preservation/accounting of the real 18-PR recovery input. Stop maintaining it after carry-in acceptance except for an actual changed-head disposition; archive as normal phase history at closure. Before import this payload/index/DAG are the local plan; after import the payload is historical import evidence and Beads is authoritative. Regenerate required DAG from that authority, never maintain another decision ledger or certificate.
E2. Tests/builds/checkers emit normal stdout/stderr, exit/results, candidate SHA, CI run/artifact links and necessary wheel hashes. U.3/U.5/U.8/U.9 consume them to detect the observed size/lint/install/legacy-behavior failures. Reuse same-head evidence; changed code/configuration or failures justify reruns. Required results and wheel artifacts must remain accessible through the independent acceptance/review that consumes them; an expired/missing run or artifact is not PASS evidence. If existing retention expires first, retain the needed artifact through existing CI controls or rerun the affected exact-candidate build/checks and use the new actual hashes, never reconstruct a certificate. Use existing CI artifact-retention policy; after final acceptance stop actively maintaining verification summaries and let scratch/log artifacts expire normally. No new evidence service, manual matrix database, duplicate proof certificate or committed reports/**. Persistent regression tests and shipped docs are product assets, not temporary evidence.
E3. Remove disposable local-index services/environments, baseline-suite overlays and temporary build/install worktrees after results are captured, on success or failure. Keep only ordinary CI results/hash links needed for the actual acceptance; no baseline fork or ongoing rehearsal infrastructure. The private rehearsal never uploads to PyPI/TestPyPI.

## Release and technical contract
0.8.5 is an explicit release gate, not assumed published. Confirm kit/native/wheel versions, helper policy/default profile/logging/artifacts support, corrected managed Python PATH, ARM64 support and packaged pytests fix from the actual released artifact before U.5/U.9. Retain packaged pytests; do not omit it to pass0.8.4. The sc-lint lead confirmed work lint-085.18/QA lint-085.19; research handoffs are in /Users/randlee/.codex/reports/sc-lint-0.8.4-adoption-plan-20261103/upstream-confirmed-reply*.txt.
Analyzer exit10 keeps ok:true/data.findings; helper exit5 has ok:false/error.details.findings, capped10 plus true findings_count. Preserve raw exit/envelope and true totals. Config errors3/usage2/profile.steps_failed failed_steps[{index,name,exit_code,message,step_log_destination?,step_log_error?}]. Version uses data.version+self_contained. Never let the consumer reporter's legacy Findings exit0 make a strict gate green.

## Sanity / scope
Read-only dev-sanity verifies numbered deliverables from existing evidence, without rerunning lint or duplicating QA. D1-D7 have explicit owners; none is assumed approved. Flaky tests are redesigned with controlled inputs, not sleeps/races/load. The user now authorizes review/fix iterations until no issues remain, followed by independent quality-mgr review. This does not create permanent review machinery. Existing approvals apply to their recorded old revisions; this local revision claims validation only, not fresh independent approval.
acceptance_criteria:
1. U.9's single authoritative aggregate checklist passes for the full exact candidate; all carried/new code, #648/#817/#820 and superseded #819 are accounted for. Unimplemented records remain open.
2. Apply root landing rules L1-L4 and evidence rules E1-E3. No duplicate landing policy on stack/sprints; U.1 has the only source-head checklist. D1-D7 decisions remain explicit.
3. Sprint index/DAG represent only actual hard prerequisites with disjoint concurrent write ownership. All sprints specify agent_level fast/normal/frontier; metadata difficulty maps frontier to installed hard without inventing model IDs.
4. This revision stays local: strict render, validate-plan, DAG regeneration and local commit only. No import/pour/push/PR/stack mutation/publish. After local review/fix convergence submit the exact final commit to quality-mgr; only that reviewer can grant new approval. Plan validation is not product execution evidence.

title: u-6: generated-cli-reference
description:

title: u-7: stable-abi-wheels
description:
## Issue/release and decisions
#820 https://github.com/randlee/sc-compose/issues/820 spans U.7 build and U.8 install validation; both are REQUIRED for 1.8.0. #819 is superseded, close when #820 lands. D4 OPEN: confirm requested CPython >=3.9 floor; D5 OPEN: do sc-sha-python and sc-composer-beads-python also go abi3? This sprint does not close #820 alone. No publishing.
## Deliverables
1. For issue #820 (FR-8 constrains deterministic results/diagnostics), after D4/D5 disposition add pyo3 abi3-py39 to sc-compose-py on the carried PyO3 0.30/#829 layer, set requires-python >=3.9 and matching metadata/classifiers if confirmed. Keep extension-module wheel linkage separate from normal Rust tests. Enable cp39-abi3 wheel builds for macOS arm64, manylinux aarch64, manylinux x86_64 and Windows amd64. U.8 builds once per platform and reuses those hashes across all install cells. Frozen #829 is not edited. If floor changes, record revised explicit tag/matrix criteria under user decision first; never claim cp39 using another floor. No new Windows ARM/macOS Intel commitment.
2. Audit bindings/python/python and stubs for Python 3.9 compatibility: runtime tomllib, evaluated X|Y annotations, imported typing APIs and packaging constraints. Use compatibility code/dependencies only where actual 3.9 execution requires it; test package import/annotations/stubs at the selected floor. Audit sibling metadata/Python/extension sources only if D5 admits them; otherwise their ABI policy remains explicit and unchanged.
3. Compile all selected extension modules with PyO3 0.30 limited API enabled and inspect symbols/tags for accidental non-limited APIs. Run cargo check -p sc-compose-py --features pyo3/abi3-py39, cargo test --workspace and built-wheel binding regressions; equivalent sibling checks are conditional on D5. A filename alone is not ABI proof. Hand U.8 the accepted package/build invocation and selected floor/package decisions; the 24-cell install matrix and index rehearsal belong to U.8.
4. Hand U.8 the accepted ABI feature/package metadata, floor/sibling decisions and built-wheel invocation/artifact contract. U.4 owns final xwin configuration and U.8 owns four-platform build-once/install validation. This sprint never edits shared lint/kit/CI files or waits for CLI-reference output. #787 remains D3 and is not bundled as a default behavior change.
design: Agent level: frontier. Own binding Cargo/pyproject files, Python runtime/stubs, limited-API feature/compile/symbol checks and Cargo.lock. Conditional sibling paths follow D5. Example after D4 confirmation: pyo3 = { version = "0.30", features = ["abi3-py39"] }; requires-python = ">=3.9"; wheel tag cp39-abi3-<platform>; extension-module remains separate for maturin. title: u-8: wheel-install-validation
description:
## Issue/release and prerequisite
#820 REQUIRED 1.8.0 scope is shared with U.7; #819 is superseded, close when #820 lands. Consume U.7's accepted ABI/package candidate and explicit D4/D5 decisions; build once per selected platform and reuse the same hashed wheel in every corresponding install cell. This sprint owns install/preflight validation, not ABI feature implementation or publication.
## Deliverables
1. In the isolated wheel-compat workflow, build once per selected platform from U.7's recorded candidate, then run the built-wheel install/import matrix for EVERY CPython 3.9,3.10,3.11,3.12,3.13,3.14 on EACH of macOS arm64, manylinux aarch64, manylinux x86_64 and Windows amd64: 24 core cells, adjusted only by an explicit D4 floor decision. Both pip and uv wheel-only resolution/install must succeed without a Rust toolchain, source-tree import or sdist fallback. Import sc_compose, verify native-extension identity and run representative deterministic composition smoke outside checkout. Record actual interpreter/platform/tag and resolved artifact hash. No unavailable/skipped cell counts as PASS; use native runners/controlled containers/VMs with the requested interpreter. Extend packages only if D5 selects siblings.
2. Add a TestPyPI-style REHEARSAL using those same built wheels, metadata and a disposable local simple-index/artifact staging service. Verify clean pip/uv wheel-only resolution/install/import for staged versioned artifacts. No TestPyPI/PyPI upload, tokens, release tags, public deployment or publishing. Controlled fixtures reject missing platform wheels, incompatible tag/floor and source fallback; no sleeps/load/event-order reliance.
3. Expose the consumer-owned script/reusable-workflow contract in design that rejects incomplete/incompatible staged wheels before publication. Automate actual native matrix jobs in .github/workflows/wheel-compat.yml, the only workflow this sprint edits. U.9 alone connects this checker/workflow to shared CI/release preflight, manifests and U.6's independently produced manual. No U.6 dependency or vendored publisher edits.
4. Hand U.9 exact candidate/artifact hashes, all installer/matrix outcomes, negative-fixture and rehearsal evidence. #820 acceptance requires both U.7 and U.8; U.9 alone updates the phase issue ledger. This sprint does not relabel/close issues, publish, or claim the final phase acceptance.
design:
Agent level: normal. Consume U.7's accepted ABI/package build contract. Build each platform wheel once, then test that same artifact through pip and uv for all six interpreters; no second build hidden in an install cell. Four platform families x six CPython versions = 24 core cells, each with two installer executions, not 24 observed failures. Siblings are conditional on D5. Run outside checkout without cargo/rustc/source fallback and assert the native module resolves to the fresh installed environment. Mac import tests directly exercise the reported source-build import failure class; the Apple linker root cause is unconfirmed. Record macOS/SDK versions: a run on another OS/SDK does not reproduce or prove resolution of that original platform-specific symptom.
Owned automation is wheel-compat.yml plus scripts/check_abi3_wheels.py and deterministic fixtures. The checker takes staged artifacts/version and emits normal exit/stdout/stderr results with artifact hashes/interpreter/platform; no separate evidence database or manually maintained matrix schema. U.9 connects it to shared release/preflight once. Local-index rehearsal stages the same built wheels in a disposable private index, sends nothing to PyPI/TestPyPI, and follows E2/E3 cleanup. Positive real install/import runs are required alongside missing-wheel/tag/floor/source-fallback negative fixtures. FR-8 protects behavior/diagnostic stability. No docs/managed-kit dependency.
Concrete consumer contract (planned interface, not an existing command): python scripts/check_abi3_wheels.py --wheel-dir <staging> --version <version> --python-floor <selected-floor> --packages <JSON-array-of-distribution-names>. Nonzero exit rejects missing platform wheels, wrong package/version/ABI-floor/tag or incompatible metadata; stdout/stderr identify the failing artifact without pretending a static check proves runtime imports. .github/workflows/wheel-compat.yml supports workflow_call (and optional manual dispatch) with required candidate-sha, version, python-floor and packages inputs (packages uses that same JSON-array encoding); it exposes the validated wheel-artifact-prefix for same-run artifact reuse. U.9 calls this exact workflow/checker and gates its jobs on the actual success result, exact candidate/version and matching wheel hashes.
Build jobs may use a fixed supported build interpreter with abi3 enabled; install jobs are distinct clean environments, with caches disabled/empty environments and no cargo/rustc on the consumer PATH. They must install via wheel-only resolution from the staged artifact/index and assert installed distribution version and native-module location. Do not use maturin develop, local editable installs, preinstalled copies or six different wheel builds to satisfy six interpreter cells. Version is the actual candidate/workspace version; a controlled 1.8.0 packaging fixture is not live release evidence. No registry credentials, release tags, publisher workflow or uploads are needed to execute this reusable validation. Siblings not selected by D5 remain outside the ABI3 claim.
acceptance_criteria:
1. For all four platform architectures x six CPython versions, pip AND uv install ONLY the one staged wheel built from the accepted U.7 candidate and import/use the installed native module outside checkout without Rust tools. All 24 core cells pass, with actual interpreter/platform/tag/hash recorded, no sdist/source fallback or skipped cells. Apply explicitly selected D4/D5 floor/sibling disposition, never an assumed narrower matrix.
2. Controlled local-index TestPyPI-style rehearsal passes with the same artifacts; missing/incompatible wheel and fallback-negative fixtures fail deterministically. No remote upload/publish/deploy/tag. The exposed staging checker rejects incomplete or incompatible wheels; actual shared preflight wiring is mandatory in U.9.
3. cargo test --workspace and targeted deterministic wheel-matrix/rehearsal/preflight fixtures pass. Actual native artifact install/import evidence is required in addition to fixture tests; no Rust build-only substitute.
4. U.9 receives complete #820 U.7+U.8 evidence for final ledger accounting; #819 stays superseded until #820 lands. Planned/released label lifecycle remains final-ledger accounting in U.9; no issue updates or publish performed here. The wheel-compat workflow actually runs the native jobs and preserves normal CI outcomes under E2. U.9 checks the same artifact/version contract after shared wiring; fixtures alone do not satisfy installation. The reusable invocation and checker reject wrong candidate/version/floor/package artifacts and cannot pass from a stale cached installation. Calling workflow/jobs are blocked on actual validation failure; normal build tooling in producer jobs is allowed but must be unavailable to install consumers.
